body.statement: For every \(\mathbf P=(P_n)\in\mathcal B_{\epsilon,M,c_0,v_0,v_1}\), \(\max\{|\inf\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}-\inf\widehat C^{\mathrm G}|,|\sup\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}-\sup\widehat C^{\mathrm G}|\}=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2})\). The same conclusion holds with \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}_{\delta_{\mathrm{num}}}\) when \(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}=o(n^{-1/2})\). Both robust intervals retain the finite-sample coverage conclusion of \(thm:global-honest-upper\) on the full class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\), including the rare-cell transition where no Gaussian approximation is imposed.
body.justification: Endpoint equivalence makes global honesty costless to first order on the regular local submodel.
body.gap: ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML, Theorem 5.1, proves uniform asymptotic validity for cross-fitted orthogonal-score intervals under nuisance-rate conditions, but does not connect such a local Gaussian benchmark to a finite-sample honest interval on the unrestricted arbitrary-mass class. The balanced lower-mass condition is imposed only on this proposal's local equivalence submodel.
body.consumer: A single reporting rule for applications whose effective dimension may be uncertain: it behaves like the standard efficient interval when justified and remains honest otherwise.
